speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in each year since 2019 (a) how many employers have informed the Ministry in writing of modifications to the salary terms for a work permit holder to less favourable terms than declared and stated in their in-principle approval letter; (b) how many employers have been fined for not having done so; (c) how many notices of salary reduction have been issued to workers; and (d) on what grounds does the Ministry determine whether a salary reduction can be allowed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is to provide flexibility for instances where the worker’s performance fell below expectation and cannot justify the salary paid.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers can check their latest salary as declared by their employers to MOM through the MyMOM portal on MOM’s website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM is also working on sending a push notification to workers via the SGWorkPass app to inform workers of any salary changes in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (the Minister for Manpower)
text: Where there is a dispute over salary reduction from the amount stated in the in-principle approval letter, the employer is required to show documented evidence of the worker’s consent and that he had notified MOM beforehand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (the Minister for Manpower)
text: Otherwise, the original declared salary holds and the employer will be required to make good any salary shortfall, regardless of the reason for the salary reduction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think he mentioned 3% of the workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, could I just ask whether MOM can review my earlier suggestion?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand that there is a need for flexibility in terms of salary reduction, but could we at least cap it?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because I know there are cases where there can be a reduction of more than 50% of their salary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I also just ask how does MOM proactively look for cases where there had been salary reduction but were not reported to MOM?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, that gives the Member a sense of the gravity of the problem, which in the grand scheme of things, is a very small number of employers that has been taken to task.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Just to ask whether we can put a cap in terms of the salary reduction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Because I know there are cases where the salary could be reduced by more than 50% which is quite significant for some of the migrant workers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, in a severe economic downturn, employers may have to cut cost significantly to save jobs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And in the instance, it may be preferable  even for the migrant worker to continue to be in employment rather than to lose his job and be repatriated.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think this is something which has to be negotiated between the employer and the employee and have  written consent, and to be notified to MOM.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And if there are disputes regarding that, this is where further reconciliation and investigation by MOM can take place.
